headings.title: Introduction and Psychological Status in Post-Abortion Care
headings.content: Post-abortion care (PAC) requires a delicate balance of clinical skill and deep emotional intelligence. Clients presenting for PAC often navigate a complex mix of relief, grief, fear, and social anxiety. Cultural and religious stigmas surrounding pregnancy termination in Nigeria frequently force women to seek care in secrecy, heightening their vulnerability and distress. A nurse must recognize that psychological trauma can manifest as physical tension, withdrawal, or defensiveness. Approaching every client with steady empathy helps lower their defense mechanisms and facilitates holistic healing.

headings.title: Core Principles of Compassionate and Non-Judgmental Care
headings.content: Providing non-judgmental care means separating personal moral convictions from professional duties. Every nurse holds personal beliefs regarding reproductive health, but projecting these values onto a vulnerable patient violates professional ethics. Compassionate care in PAC involves validating the client's physical pain without interrogating their personal choices. When a nurse maintains a neutral, supportive demeanor, the client feels safe enough to disclose vital health history without fear of reprimand.

headings.title: Effective Communication and Active Listening
headings.content:
Communication in PAC extends far beyond asking routine medical questions. Active listening requires the nurse to pay attention to non-verbal cues such as avoiding eye contact, trembling hands, or forced silence. 

- **Open-ended phrasing**: Encourages the client to narrate their experience in their own words.
- **Reflective feedback**: Demonstrates to the client that their feelings are heard and acknowledged.
- **Calm tone of voice**: Reduces the client's autonomic nervous system arousal during a stressful physical examination.

headings.title: Establishing Trust, Rapport, and Confidentiality
headings.content: Trust forms the bedrock of any therapeutic nurse-client relationship. In PAC, maintaining strict confidentiality is both an ethical mandate and a clinical necessity. If a client suspects that their medical record or personal story will be shared casually among ward staff or outside the hospital, they may withhold critical symptoms or refuse follow-up care. Introducing yourself clearly, explaining every procedure before touching the client, and reassuring them of privacy safeguards builds immediate rapport.

headings.title: Navigating Cultural Sensitivities and Personal Bias
headings.content: Nigerian healthcare settings blend diverse ethnic beliefs, religious doctrines, and traditional practices regarding reproductive health. A nurse must navigate these sensitivities without imposing personal biases. A common pitfall is assuming every client shares the nurse's specific moral or religious viewpoint. Providing standardized, high-quality care regardless of tribe, religion, or social standing ensures equitable health delivery and protects client dignity.

headings.title: Post-Abortion Counseling and Contraceptive Advice
headings.content: Counseling in PAC is not about preaching or coercing the client into a specific lifestyle choice. Instead, it is an empowering dialogue aimed at preventing future unintended pregnancies and promoting physical recovery. Contraceptive information must be presented objectively, detailing benefits, potential side effects, and correct usage for each method. The nurse assesses the client's readiness, respects their autonomy in decision-making, and provides supplies or referrals before discharge.
